newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah strengthens on band speculation.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah strengthens on band speculation.

text.p: The rupiah strengthened against the dollar in late trading on Thursday on speculation that the central bank intervention band would be widened, dealers said.
They said the fresh speculation, which emanated from Singapore, briefly drove the rupiah below the 2,432.0 resistance level before the dollar made a rebound.
"Offshore operators seem to be trying to launch another test on the band. But the attempts were half-hearted, reflected by the quick rebound of the dollar after the fixing," one said.
Spot rupiah settled at 2,431.75/32.25 at 0820 GMT after rising to a high of 2,430.50 from an opening of 2,433.0/33.5.
Dealers said the dollar bounced back immediately after the central bank kept its intervention band unchanged at 2,427/2,619 and the conversion band at 2,427/2,475 in the afternoon fixing.
"This seems to suggest the market is not really convinced the central bank will widen its band soon," another said.

One local bank dealer said some offshore banks tried to reduce losses arising from false positioning of the baht and the rupiah. He said some players had gone short on dollars when the rupiah was hit by worries of a baht devaluation.

The rupiah fell to a low of 2,445 on Wednesday on offshore selling on rumours of a baht devaluation. The rupiah recovered as Thailand announced a managed float policy although that was understood as a de facto devaluation by analysts.
"Although the rupiah recovered, but the losses were there," the dealer said, adding that the fresh speculation of a band widening was designed to recover some of the losses.
Today rupiah closed at 2,431.5/32.0. There was no trade in value tomorrow due to a public holiday in the United States on Friday.
Dealers said increased speculation of a widening was due to the Consultative Group for Indonesia (CGI) donor meeting in Tokyo later this month chaired by the World Bank.
The bank said in a report on Indonesia last month that some countries had a wider intervention band but did not specifically suggest that Jakarta follow suit.
But central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said it was not good sense to follow what other people were doing.
"This kind of argument is weak. That is not good economic policy that just because other poeple have 15 percent we have to go to 15 percent," Djiwandono said.
One currency analyst said he did not expect a band widening in the near term because it would appreciate the rupiah and thus be counter-productive to the sluggish export recovery.

He said the central bank would not want to be made responsible for the country's export performance due to its exchange rate policy while the rupiah was not under heavy pressure for an immediate fine-tuning.

One European bank dealer explained strong rupiah support from the stock market point of view. He said portfolio inflows had also put pressure on the dollar as reflected by the stock market index which has hit three new highs this week.
Overnight swap was at 1.75/1.85 and spot/next at 0.27/0.33.
One-month swaps were at 12.25/12.75, two at 25.5/27.0, three at 38.0/39.0 and six at 79.5/80.5 points.
